CausalChain: Chronic inflammation -> Activation of CAFs -> ECM remodeling and increased stiffness -> Enhanced mechanotransduction (YAP/TAZ activation) -> Induction of EMT and acquisition of CSC properties -> Increased chemoresistance in cholangiocarcinoma
Hypothesis: In cholangiocarcinoma, CAF-mediated ECM stiffening activates YAP/TAZ signaling, which drives EMT and cancer stem cell–like transformation, contributing to chemoresistance; therefore, inhibiting YAP/TAZ mechanotransduction can be a viable therapeutic strategy to overcome drug resistance.
Abstract: We propose that in cholangiocarcinoma the tumor microenvironment, particularly the activity of cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs), plays a pivotal role in driving chemoresistance through mechanical remodeling. Chronic inflammatory stimuli activate CAFs, which in turn remodel the extracellular matrix (ECM), increasing its stiffness. This stiffened ECM enhances mechanotransduction pathways in tumor cells, notably through YAP/TAZ activation. The resultant signaling cascade promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and endows cholangiocarcinoma cells with stem cell–like features, thereby contributing to intrinsic and acquired chemoresistance. Therapeutically targeting YAP/TAZ mechanotransduction may disrupt this cascade and improve drug sensitivity.
